title: Interface Control of Second-Harmonic Generation in Layered CuInP2S6 via PbZr0.2Ti0.8O3 Domain Wall
authors: Dawei Li, Juhe Liu, Yifei Hao, Qiuchen Wu, Xi Huang, Jesse Stebbing, Xinyi Hou, Gaolei Zhao, Kun Wang, Yongfeng Lu, Xia Hong
abstract: The control of nonlinear optical responses in van der Waals ferroelectrics at the nanoscale offers opportunities for developing two-dimensional integrated nanophotonics with programmable functionalities. In this work, we report the first realization of nanoscale nonvolatile control of the amplitude and polarization of second-harmonic generation (SHG) response in layered CuInP2S6 (CIPS) via the domain structure in an interfacial PbZr0.2Ti0.8O3 (PZT) thin film. The SHG intensity at CIPS/PZT heterointerface is continuously modulated, either substantially enhanced or almost entirely quenched, by the circular domain walls in underlying ferroelectric oxide. The interfacial coupling of CIPS polar axis with in-plane polarization of PZT domain walls tailors the SHG light polarization into two-fold (C2V) symmetry, which is well modeled by nonlinear electromagnetic theory. Overall, this study enables nonvolatile programmable design of nonlinear light intensity and polarization in van der Waals ferroelectrics at the nanoscale.
summary: This paper reports the first realization of nonvolatile, nanoscale control over Second-Harmonic Generation (SHG) in layered CIPS by interfacing it with patterned ferroelectric domain walls in PZT. By utilizing the domain structure, the SHG intensity and polarization can be deterministically modulated, enabling programmable design of nonlinear light sources at the nanoscale.
main_problem: The research aims to achieve nanoscale, nonvolatile control over the amplitude and polarization of Second-Harmonic Generation (SHG) in layered CuInP2S6 (CIPS).
main_result: The SHG signal is continuously modulated (enhanced or quenched) by the domain walls in the underlying ferroelectric PbZr0.2Ti0.8O3 (PZT), allowing for programmable control of nonlinear light properties.
method: The study uses nonlinear optical microscopy to measure SHG, correlating the signal changes with the polarization state of ferroelectric domain walls characterized by PFM.
model_or_system: The physical system is a CIPS/PZT heterointerface, where the ferroelectric domain structure of PZT acts as the control element for the nonlinear optical response of the van der Waals ferroelectric CIPS.
key_observables: SHG intensity and polarization, which are modulated by the relative orientation between the CIPS polar axis and the PZT domain wall polarization.
important_parameters: The thickness of the CIPS flake (e.g., 9-50 nm) and the relative angle ($	heta$) between the CIPS polar axis and the PZT domain wall polarization are critical parameters.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the SHG response is dominated by the interfacial coupling between the CIPS polar axis and the in-plane polarization of the PZT domain walls.
figures_summary: Figures show SHG mapping and polar plots demonstrating the dependence of the SHG signal on the incident light polarization angle ($\varphi$) and the domain wall polarization ($	heta$).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the platform using PFM/AFM to map domain structures, followed by SHG measurements to quantify the nonlinear optical response, and finally, theoretical modeling confirms the dependence on polarization alignment.
why_interesting: This work demonstrates electrical/structural control over nonlinear optical responses in 2D materials, which is highly relevant to developing integrated quantum photonic devices or advanced light sources.
